q: 1. The method in which different types of refuse are collected, carried and disposed off separately is called
explain: The conservancy system (dry system) involves manual collection and separate disposal of different wastes (human excreta vs. garbage).

q: 2. The pipe through which liquid waste carrying human excreta flows, is called
explain: A soil pipe is the plumbing component designed specifically to carry discharge from WCs (water closets) or urinals.

q: 3. The most suitable excreta disposal unit for human excreta is
explain: A privy pit (latrine pit) is a basic and common method for the direct disposal of human excreta in areas without a piped sewerage system.

q: 4. In high rate activated sludge treatment, bacteria are removed from
explain: Activated sludge plants are highly efficient, typically achieving 80-95% removal of bacteria and BOD.

q: 5. Biological action is used in
explain: Trickling filters rely on a biological slime layer (biofilm) of aerobic bacteria to consume organic contaminants.

q: 6. A septic tank is a
options: combination of sedimentation and digestion tank
explain: A septic tank performs two functions: it allows solids to settle (sedimentation) and then allows anaerobic bacteria to break them down (digestion).

q: 7. The effluents from the septic tank are discharged into
explain: Because septic tank effluent is still partially polluted, it is typically discharged into a soak pit or dispersion trench for ground absorption.

q: 8. Land disposal of sewage will be favorable where
options: the rivers run dry or have a small flow during summer
climate is wet and rates of evaporation is low
explain: Land disposal (irrigation) is preferred when the receiving water bodies do not have enough volume (dilution capacity) to handle the sewage.

q: 9. Disposal by dilution will be suitable where
options: the sewage arriving at the out fall points is fresh
explain: Dilution works best when water is moving away, not returning to the shore, and when the sewage is fresh (hasn't become septic/odorous).

q: 10. The natural process in which the oxygen of water of streams is consumed and replenished by the atmosphere is
explain: Self-purification is the natural ability of a river to recover its dissolved oxygen and water quality through physical and biological processes.

q: 11. The activated sludge
explain: Activated sludge is rich in nutrients (N and P), its color/smell indicates aeration levels, and it typically has a very high water content (>95%).

q: 12. Sludge treatment is mainly done in order of
explain: The goals of sludge treatment are to make it non-putrescible (stable), kill germs, and reduce its volume for easier disposal.

q: 13. The effluent of a biological treatment unit should have a B.O.D. less than
explain: Standard secondary treatment regulations (like the Royal Commission Standard) often require an effluent BOD of 30 mg/L or less.

q: 14. The effluent from the lime soda process contains a hardness of ............
explain: Unlike the zeolite process, the lime-soda process cannot reduce hardness to zero; it typically leaves a residual hardness of about 50 mg/l.

q: 15. Conservation system is best suited ............
explain: The 'Conservancy' (dry) system involves manual collection and removal of waste, which is only economically feasible where labor is very inexpensive.

q: 16. A deplorable aspect of conservancy system is ............
options: vehicles are required to carry night soil
vast areas for disposal are necessary
human elements is involved in collection and transportation of human waste
explain: The most criticized aspect is the 'manual scavenging' or human involvement in handling raw sewage, which is unhygienic and undignified.

q: 17. Water carriage system needs more ............
explain: As the name suggests, the water carriage system uses water as the medium to transport waste through sewers, requiring a significant volume of water to function.

q: 18. The bacteria that flourish at high temperature (greater than 45°C) are called ............
explain: Thermophilic bacteria are 'heat-loving' organisms used in high-temperature sludge digestion processes to speed up decomposition.

q: 19. Aerobic bacteria ............
options: produce less energy and more end products
explain: Aerobic bacteria require dissolved oxygen to survive; movement (aeration) keeps oxygen levels high, whereas stagnant water quickly becomes depleted of oxygen.

q: 20. Anaerobes give out ............
explain: Anaerobic decomposition is less efficient than aerobic; it produces unstable intermediate compounds like organic acids and gases (CH4, H2S) that are highly odorous.

q: 21. The common end products for both aerobiosis and anaerobiosis is ............
explain: Carbon dioxide is the ultimate stable oxidized form of carbon and is released in both types of biological decomposition.

q: 22. A unit working purely on anaerobiosis is ............
explain: A septic tank is an enclosed, airtight chamber where solids settle and undergo anaerobic digestion without the presence of dissolved oxygen.

q: 23. Anaerobic treatment is best suited for ............
explain: Anaerobic processes (like sludge digesters) are ideal for concentrated organic waste because they don't require the massive energy input of aeration needed for aerobic treatment.

q: 24. A natural method of disposal of sewage is ............
explain: Applying sewage directly to land (irrigation) uses the natural filtering capacity of soil and biological action of soil microbes to treat the waste.

q: 25. Sewage farming is best suited for Nepal because ............
options: it is a cheap method of sewage disposal
nutrients and trace elements required by plants are available in sewage
explain: Sewage contains Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium (NPK). In agricultural regions, this 'liquid fertilizer' provides essential nutrients for crop growth.

q: 26. A septic tank is a water tight tank where the following operation(s) take place ............
options: decomposition of organic and inorganic matter by bacteria
explain: Septic tanks provide two-stage treatment: first, solids settle (sedimentation), and second, the settled solids are broken down by bacteria in the absence of air (anaerobic digestion).

q: 27. Mostly adopted detention period for a septic tank is ............
explain: A 24-hour detention period is the standard design to ensure adequate time for both settling and the start of biological activity.

q: 28. The gases given out of a septic tank are ............
explain: Anaerobic digestion produces a mixture of Carbon Dioxide, Methane (fuel gas), and Hydrogen Sulphide (the source of the smell).

q: 29. Septic tanks are best suited for ............
explain: Septic tanks are an on-site sanitation solution. They are ideal for isolated or scattered houses where a centralized underground sewerage system is not economically feasible.

q: 30. Septic tank effluent is ............
options: having fine organic solids with high B.O.D.
black tarry liquor with earthen odour
explain: The effluent from a septic tank still contains significant organic matter and pathogens. It usually has a high Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) and requires further treatment in a soak pit or leach field.

q: 31. Media used in trickling filter is ............
explain: The filter media must be 'inert' (non-reactive) and tough to support the weight of the biofilm and the flow of sewage without breaking down.

q: 32. Usual size of media in standard rate trickling filter is ............
explain: Standard rate filters use larger media (25-100mm) to ensure large enough voids to prevent clogging from the growth of biological slime (zoogleal film).

q: 33. Depth of standard rate trickling filter is ............
explain: Trickling filters are generally deep enough to allow for sufficient contact time between the sewage and the biofilm; 1.5 to 4.8m is the common design range.

q: 34. Biological layer stickling to the trickling filter media consists of ............
explain: The 'zoogleal film' is a complex ecosystem containing various microorganisms like bacteria, fungi, and protozoa that feed on the organic matter in sewage.

q: 35. An extension of trickling filter is ............
explain: A Bio-tower is essentially a very tall trickling filter (up to 12m or more) using lightweight plastic media instead of stone.

q: 36. The primary operations in a trickling filter are ............
explain: Organic matter is first adsorbed/absorbed by the biological film and then broken down (oxidized) by the aerobic bacteria within that film.

q: 37. A very important character is media of a trickling filter is ............
explain: The more surface area available per unit volume, the more bacteria can grow, leading to higher treatment efficiency.

q: 38. Recirculation ratio for a standard rate trickling filter is ............
explain: Standard rate filters typically do not use recirculation; the sewage passes through the filter only once.

q: 39. A high rate biological treatment unit has a F/M ratio of ............
explain: The Food-to-Microorganism (F/M) ratio for conventional high-rate systems generally falls between 0.2 and 0.5 for stable operation.

q: 40. Effluent from a high rate trickling filter is ............
options: well nitrified and free from odours
explain: High-rate filters process sewage faster, which means the effluent is often less nitrified and slightly more turbid/brown compared to standard rate filters.

q: 41. Psychoda alternata is found in ............
explain: Psychoda alternata (the Filter Fly) is a common nuisance pest that breeds in the moist, organic environment of trickling filters.

q: 42. Filter unloading is ............
explain: Also known as 'sloughing', this is the process where the biological film becomes too heavy and detaches from the media, washing out with the effluent.

q: 43. To improve efficiency recirculation of the following is done in H.R. trickling filters ............
explain: In High-Rate filters, a portion of the treated effluent is pumped back to the inlet to dilute high-strength waste and keep the filter wet.

q: 44. The immediate layer sticking to the media of a trickling filter is of ............
explain: While the outer surface of the slime is aerobic, the layer directly touching the media is starved of oxygen and becomes anaerobic.

q: 45. An equivalent term of 'Mean cell residence time' is ............
explain: Mean Cell Residence Time (MCRT) is essentially the same as Solids Retention Time (SRT), representing the average time the bacteria stay in the system.

q: 46. In operation a R.B.C. is nearer to ............
explain: Like a trickling filter, RBC is an 'attached growth' system where the microbes stay fixed to a surface rather than floating in the water.

q: 47. Activated sludge process is a biological process involving ............
explain: ASP is a 'suspended growth' process that uses a diverse community of aerobic organisms to break down waste in an oxygen-rich environment.

q: 48. Media provided in A.S.P. is ............
explain: ASP does not use fixed media. The bacteria are kept in suspension through mechanical agitation or air bubbling.

q: 49. Efficiency of activated sludge process is ............
explain: When properly operated, ASP is highly efficient, typically removing 90-95% of the BOD from the influent sewage.

q: 50. Conventional ASP is not suited to ............
options: strong loading and varying quality of influent
shock loading and varying quality of influent
explain: Conventional ASP is sensitive; a 'shock' of toxic chemicals or a sudden surge in volume can kill the bacteria or wash them out of the system.
